patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — PrestaShop and VTEX share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Frame: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — PrestaShop and VTEX share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.. Choose PrestaShop only if your buying job matches “Open-source PHP commerce — Classic free; Hosted from ~$26/mo annual (€24 excl. VAT) with 1” rather than VTEX's shape. Choose VTEX only if your buying job matches “Enterprise commerce SaaS — contact-sales get-started only; no invented floors. Shopify kee” rather than PrestaShop's shape. Workflow advantage: PrestaShop leans catalog-management; VTEX leans wholesale-b2b. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — PrestaShop and VTEX share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: PrestaShop is Open-source PHP commerce — Classic free; Hosted from ~$26/mo annual (€24 excl. VAT) with 14-day trial; Enterprise quote. WooCommerce keeps t; VTEX is Enterprise commerce SaaS — contact-sales get-started only; no invented floors. Shopify keeps the SaaS award..
- Company-size focus: PrestaShop (small-business, mid-market) vs VTEX (mid-market, enterprise).
- Workflow coverage skew: PrestaShop-leaning catalog-management vs VTEX-leaning wholesale-b2b.
- Researched limits: PrestaShop — Classic TCO (hosting, modules, agency) is not $0 even when the license is free; VTEX — No published self-serve monthly tiles — hard to shortlist on list price alone.

Limitations — PrestaShop: Classic TCO (hosting, modules, agency) is not $0 even when the license is free; POS / omnichannel is module-dependent, not a native retail bundle; VTEX: No published self-serve monthly tiles — hard to shortlist on list price alone; Enterprise sales and implementation cycles versus Shopify SMB speed.

Poor-fit cases: PrestaShop is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Classic TCO (hosting, modules, agency) is not $0 even when the license is free · VTEX is a poor fit when that limitation bites: No published self-serve monthly tiles — hard to shortlist on list price alone · Avoid PrestaShop if you actually need VTEX's motion (Enterprise commerce SaaS — contact-sales get-started only; no invented floors. S)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
